evals.prompt: I chair the governance committee at Hearth & Home, a $4.5M supportive housing nonprofit in Portland, Maine. We have 11 board members; 3 terms end in June 2027. Our new strategic plan prioritizes a capital campaign for a 40-unit building and deeper resident voice. Right now we're mostly bankers and retired clergy, all white, all over 55. How should we recruit for those 3 seats?
evals.expected_output: A matrix-driven recruitment process: build a skills/access/representation matrix, identify gaps against the strategic plan, write target profiles before naming names, source 3–5 candidates per seat, cultivate in stages, use a letter of expectation, check terms against bylaws, and onboard before the first vote.
assertions: Builds or outlines a board matrix with expertise, access/capacity, and representation bands, including lived experience with the population served (e.g., current or former residents)
Ties gap priorities to the strategic plan, e.g., real estate/facilities and major-gift/fundraising capacity for the capital campaign and resident/lived-experience representation
Writes a target profile for each seat naming 2–3 gap attributes before identifying candidates
Recommends sourcing 3–5 candidates per open seat, including people already close to the mission (volunteers, program alumni, donors), and tracking stage like a pipeline
Describes cultivation before the ask (informational meeting, observe a meeting or serve on a committee) and preparing a letter of expectation before the ask
Includes an onboarding packet before the first vote (e.g., bylaws, budget, Form 990, strategic plan, conflict-of-interest policy to sign) and checks terms/election against the bylaws text

evals.prompt: can u draft a letter of expectation for new board members? we're a small arts org, $350k budget, board meets 6x/yr, we do give-or-get of $1,000
evals.expected_output: A filled-in letter of expectation covering role/term, time, fundraising, fiduciary duties, conflict of interest, confidentiality, onboarding, and what the member can expect, with placeholders for bylaw references.
assertions: Includes role and term with a reference to the bylaws/policy section, flagged as a placeholder to verify against the bylaws
States the time commitment (6 meetings/year, committee assignment, hours per month)
Describes fiduciary duties of care, loyalty and obedience
Covers conflict-of-interest disclosure/recusal, confidentiality, onboarding (orientation date, peer mentor), and what the organization provides, plus a signature line

evals.prompt: Our founder-ED wants to put her two closest friends on the board next month because 'we need warm bodies fast' — we're down to 5 members. Also, half our board has served 15+ years and nobody wants term limits. And honestly our board meetings are a mess — no agendas, committees don't meet. Can you fix all of this?
evals.expected_output: Warns against relationship-first recruiting, offers a fast matrix and bench approach, frames term limits as a staggered rotation policy drafted with bylaws/policy work, and routes meeting and committee dysfunction to board governance.
assertions: Names the risk of relationship-first recruiting (groupthink, redundant skills, shallow bench) and recommends mapping each candidate to a written matrix gap
Recommends a governance committee with a year-round recruitment charge and 3+ names per seat
Frames term limits as a staggered rotation policy rather than 'everyone must leave,' weighing institutional knowledge against disengagement
Routes drafting term-limit language to the bylaws/policy skill
Routes seated-board issues (agendas, committees, meeting function) to the board governance skill rather than handling them as recruitment

should_not_trigger.query: We need committee charters and a board self-assessment for our seated board — where do we start?
Write a position description for weekend food pantry sorting volunteers.
